prompt:
A high-fidelity design comp of a desktop website home page laid out as a horizontal scrolling comic strip. The browser viewport fills the frame edge to edge: no browser chrome, no device frame, no desk, no hands, no poster mounting.

LAYOUT, stated top to bottom. (1) A fixed album-yellow rail across the full width of the top, about twelve percent of the page height, with a black rule beneath it: at the left ADAM WORLEY hand-lettered in upright black capitals with SOFTWARE ENGINEER small beneath, and at the right an adventure-red button with black outline reading GET IN TOUCH. (2) Below the rail, occupying the entire remaining height, ONE continuous horizontal band of large square comic panels running left to right, each bounded by the same even black line with a narrow paper-white gutter, three and a half panels visible before the right edge crops the fourth mid-panel to signal horizontal scrolling. Panel one: a desk seen from behind the chair, a man shown only from behind at a keyboard, two monitors, a window with a sky-blue London skyline; an album-yellow caption box in its upper left with two lines of narration. Panel two: a steel-blue server rack beside an infrastructure diagram of boxes and connecting lines, with a white speech balloon reading TERRAFORM, GO, CONTAINERS. Panel three: an office tower facade under a flat sky-blue sky with a small caption box reading NETWEALTH. Panel four, cropped at the right edge: an indoor climbing wall with coloured holds, only its left third visible. (3) Along the very bottom edge, a thin horizontal progress rail in steel blue with a short paper-white indicator at its left end, and small chapter dots evenly spaced along it.

STYLE: ligne claire clear-line comic album artwork. One even unvarying black outline on every single shape, flat unmodulated colour fills, absolutely no gradients, no cast shadows, no shading, no texture, no photorealism, no 3D. Strict palette: sky blue, sand ochre, album yellow, paper white, sea green, steel blue, and one adventure red used sparingly. Headings hand-lettered in upright capitals; body text in clean small legible capitals.
